messages:
maria: Hey team — noticed a big jump in reserved GPU hours for our dedicated pool (pool-123) overnight but token burn stayed tiny. Dashboard shows ~78.5h consumed between 04/01 02:00-06:00 UTC but total tokens ~9.8k. Can you triage?

emma: thanks for flagging — could you paste the pool id and approximate window? i'll loop in billing and infra.

maria: pool-123, roughly 2026-04-01T02:00:00Z -> 2026-04-01T06:00:00Z. we rolled a model_variant change ~01:50 UTC (model: open-xl -> open-xl-quant). requests afterwards were low (a couple health pings + canary traffic).

emma: @sanjay @ivan bringing billing + infra on this. billing-bot: recording incident.

billing-bot: Ticket created: BILL-9302 (reserved-hours vs token discrepancy) — tagging billing oncall.

sanjay: quick question — are these hours showing as "reserved" vs "burst" on the invoice?

maria: dashboard labels them reserved-pool uptime, not burst. the billing export rows show instance_uptime attributed to the reserved_pool id.

ivan: can you share one example request id or a short time-range so we can pull instance start/stop events from metering?

maria: i grabbed one request-id from a health check: req_0a9f3b. It lands in the logs at 2026-04-01T02:05:13Z.

ivan: thx. pulling metering events now. here's a short dump from s3 (sanitized):

```
{"ts":"2026-04-01T02:00:05Z","event":"instance_start","pool":"pool-123","instance_id":"i-0a1","reason":"deploy-warmup","variant":"open-xl-quant","actor":"orchestrator"}
{"ts":"2026-04-01T02:01:10Z","event":"instance_ready","instance_id":"i-0a1","active_tokens":12}
{"ts":"2026-04-01T03:15:55Z","event":"instance_restart","instance_id":"i-0a2","reason":"oom-reclaim","variant":"open-xl-quant"}
{"ts":"2026-04-01T03:16:02Z","event":"instance_start","instance_id":"i-0a2","reason":"oom-recover","pool":"pool-123"}
{"ts":"2026-04-01T05:58:20Z","event":"instance_terminate","instance_id":"i-0a1","uptime_seconds":12045}
```

ivan: notes — several long-lived instance_start -> terminate windows with very low active_tokens. autoscaler didn't scale in; instances maintained for warmup/kv-cache reasons. the metering pipeline attributes whole uptime to reserved pool.

sanjay: looking at billing pipeline: currently we turn uptime into billed-hours at hour-granularity and attribute to pool attached to the instance. there's a recent change in metering that counts any instance with "deploy-warmup" as reserved rather than checking the pool tagging. iirc that change rolled 2026-03-31.

emma: interesting. @ivan do we have evidence these instances were pinned and not serving user-visible traffic?

ivan: yes — logs show the majority of requests were internal pings + low-token canary. KV cache prefetch triggered long warmups that keep the model loaded. memory pressure caused a restart at ~03:15, which triggered another 10m warmup. net effect = lots of instance uptime but tiny token burn.

sanjay: that explains tokens vs hours mismatch. two follow-ups: 1) billing remedy (credits) and 2) infra fix so warmup instances don't get billed as reserved hours when token activity is below threshold.

emma: for triage, please run this repro so we can confirm:

```
# repro (sanitized)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Pool: pool-123" \
  -d '{"model":"open-xl-quant","input":"ping","prefetch_kv":true}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate

# then force a memory pressure to trigger restart (internal fixture)
kubectl -n pool-123 exec deploy/warmup-fixture -- /bin/sh -c "stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 80% --timeout 60s"
```

ivan: thanks — running in a canary cluster now. initial result: warmup fixture keeps instance alive ~8-10m with low token counts. will collect metering events.

sanjay: on billing side i'll open a credit review. Maria — we may need an invoice-level manual adjustment if pipeline misattributed hours. Can you confirm whether you want a provisional credit while infra investigates?

maria: yes please — provisional credit would be great. we were hit hard on this account.

sanjay: acknowledged. i created a provisional credit request CREDIT-447 for pool-123; billing team will evaluate.

emma: infra remediation options i see: 1) revert the metering change that forces deploy-warmup => reserved attribution, 2) change metering to apply a tokens-per-hour threshold (e.g., >1000 tok/hr) before attributing reserved billing, 3) update autoscaler to use idle_ttl=300s for warmup variants. Which should we do short-term?

ivan: short term we can revert the metering attribution change (quick rollback) and flip autoscaler idle_ttl for the pool. mid-term we should add a noise-filter step to metering that verifies active_tokens over sliding window before converting uptime to billed-hours.

emma: agree. timeline: ivan to rollback metering change (ETA 2h), update autoscaler for pool-123 (ETA 1h), sanjay to post provisional credit (ETA 24h verification). i'll keep this thread updated.

ivan: rollback started — applying v2-metrics patch. monitoring metering write path for errors.

billing-bot: CREDIT-447 status: pending (assigned to billing_ops).

maria: thanks everyone. one ask — can you add an alert so we detect reserved-hours >> token-burn deviations automatically? would save us future surprise.

emma: good call. ivan — can you add an alert rule: reserved_hours / (token_count/1000) > 10 for >30m?

ivan: yep — adding rule to pool-123 alerting (will surface to #eng-sre).

sanjay: billing note: if metering rollback removes the spurious attributions, those hours will be reconciled on next export; otherwise we'll issue manual adjustments.

ivan: update — rollback finished, metering pipeline now checks pool tag + active_tokens window before attribution. initial reprocessed batch removed ~61.2h attributed to pool-123 in that window (pending final verification).

emma: excellent. maria — i'll follow up once billing confirms credit. leaving thread open until invoice reconciliation complete. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all, much appreciated.
